trip.name: Yuval & Luciana in Japan
trip.description: The real itinerary. Arrive Tokyo Sep 19, then 10 stops incl. Atami/Izu before the Tokyo finale. Attractions/food/shopping entries are starter suggestions per zone — edit freely in the app or in this file.

zones.name: Hakone
zones.summary: Onsen town in the mountains — hot springs, the Hakone loop and (weather permitting) Mt. Fuji views over Lake Ashi.

zones.name: Fujikawaguchiko
zones.summary: Lake Kawaguchi at the foot of Mt. Fuji — the classic postcard views.

zones.name: Matsumoto
zones.summary: Castle town in the Japanese Alps — one-night stop between Fuji and Takayama.

zones.name: Takayama
zones.summary: Beautifully preserved old town in the Hida mountains — morning markets and Hida beef.

zones.name: Kanazawa
zones.summary: Edo-period districts, one of Japan's top three gardens, and a great food market.

zones.name: Kyoto
zones.summary: Temples, gardens, geisha districts and old streets — four full days.

zones.name: Osaka
zones.summary: Japan's kitchen — neon, street food and day-trip base (Nara, Kobe, Himeji).

zones.name: Tokyo
zones.summary: Arrival city and grand finale — Shinjuku, Shibuya, Asakusa and everything in between.

zones.name: Atami / Izu
zones.summary: Seaside onsen town on the Izu peninsula — ocean-view hot springs, kaiseki dinners and a slow wind-down before the Tokyo finale.

places.name: Hakone Yutowa
places.description: Sep 25 – 27 · Hakone · Booking.com, confirmed, free cancellation, ₪1,920. Modern ryokan in Gora. Booking.com is offering an upgrade to a superior room WITH PRIVATE BATH, which implies the booked room may not have one — check and consider upgrading.

places.name: Mizno Hotel
places.description: Sep 27 – 28 · Fujikawaguchiko · Booking.com, confirmed, free cancellation, ₪810. One night before the Chureito sunrise. Upgrade offered to a superior room with balcony (lake/Fuji view). Confirm parking (you'll have the rental car) and ask about a very early checkout for the sunrise start.

places.name: Onyado Nono Matsumoto Natural Hot Spring
places.description: Sep 28 – 29 · Matsumoto · Booking.com, confirmed, free cancellation, ₪470. Natural hot spring baths, tatami-style, excellent value. Arrange takkyubin (luggage forwarding) here — bags go ahead to Takayama since you can't bring them into Kamikochi.

places.name: HOTEL WOOD TAKAYAMA
places.description: Sep 29 – Oct 1 · Takayama · Booking.com, confirmed, free cancellation, ₪935. You arrive here tired after the Kamikochi traverse. Confirm parking and whether dinner is included — you'll want it after that day.

places.name: The HOTEL SANRAKU KANAZAWA
places.description: Oct 1 – 3 · Kanazawa · Booking.com, confirmed, free cancellation, ₪1,664. Return the rental car THE DAY YOU ARRIVE (Oct 1), not the next day — Kanazawa is entirely walkable and parking costs money. Refuel before drop-off.

places.name: Mitsui Garden Hotel Kyoto Shinmachi Bettei
places.name_ja: 三井ガーデンホテル京都新町別邸
places.description: Oct 3 – 7 · Kyoto · Booking.com, confirmed, free cancellation, ₪2,531. Machiya-style hotel on Shinmachi street, CENTRAL Kyoto — great for Nishiki, Gion and Pontocho, but a metro ride (not a 7-min walk) from teamLab Biovortex near the station.

places.name: Candeo Hotels Osaka Shinsaibashi
places.name_ja: カンデオホテルズ大阪心斎橋
places.description: Oct 7 – 10 · Osaka · Booking.com, confirmed, ₪2,056. Excellent Shinsaibashi location, steps from Dotonbori. Candeo's signature is a top-floor sky spa — check whether it's included. In-room washing machine, good for a laundry night.

places.name: Hotel Gracery Shinjuku
places.name_ja: ホテルグレイスリー新宿
places.description: Sep 19 – 25 & Oct 12 – 16 · Tokyo (Shinjuku) · Booking.com, confirmed, free cancellation, ₪3,233. The Godzilla-head hotel in Kabukicho — covers both the arrival leg and the final leg. Ask for a high floor away from the street; Kabukicho is loud until 3–4am.

places.name: Owakudani
places.description: Volcanic valley on the Hakone ropeway — sulfur vents and the famous black eggs.

places.name: Hakone Open-Air Museum
places.description: Sculptures in the mountains, Picasso pavilion, and a foot bath.

places.name: Lake Kawaguchi
places.description: Lakeside walk and the Panoramic Ropeway; best Fuji reflections early morning.

places.name: Chureito Pagoda
places.description: THE Fuji photo spot — pagoda + Fuji in one frame. ~400 steps up; 20 min by train from Kawaguchiko.

places.name: Matsumoto Castle
places.description: One of Japan's most beautiful original castles — the black 'Crow Castle'. Evening light-up is lovely.

places.name: Sanmachi Suji old town
places.description: Preserved Edo-period streets — sake breweries, craft shops. Combine with the Miyagawa morning market by the river.

places.name: Kenroku-en Garden
places.description: One of Japan's three great gardens — go right at opening for near-empty paths. Kanazawa Castle is next door.

places.name: Higashi Chaya District
places.description: Geisha teahouse district — gold-leaf everything, including gold-leaf ice cream.

places.name: Omicho Market
places.description: Kanazawa's kitchen since 1721 — seafood breakfast (kaisendon) is the move.

places.name: Fushimi Inari Shrine
places.description: The thousand vermillion torii gates. Open 24h — sunrise or after 17:00 beats the crowds; full loop ~2h.

places.name: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove
places.description: Bamboo forest walk — combine with Tenryu-ji temple and the monkey park. Go before 08:30.

places.name: Kinkaku-ji (Golden Pavilion)
places.description: The gold-leaf pavilion over its mirror pond. 30–45 min visit; pairs well with Ryoan-ji rock garden nearby.

places.name: Nishiki Market
places.description: 'Kyoto's kitchen' — knives, pickles, matcha sweets, street snacks. No eating while walking.

places.name: Matcha stop in Gion
places.description: Placeholder pick — matcha parfait/tea house in Gion; expect queues after 11:00.

places.name: Universal Studios Japan
places.name_ja: ユニバーサル・スタジオ・ジャパン
places.description: Oct 8 — our full USJ day (Halloween season + the park's 25th anniversary). Tickets go on sale ~2 months ahead — expect Aug 8–14, 2026 — and you must buy the day they open: there are NO ticket booths at the park anymore (online only, via Klook). Get 2× Studio Pass + 2× Universal Express Pass Premium for Oct 8. The day-by-day plan is in the schedule; the complete guide we made is attached below.

places.name: Dotonbori at night
places.description: Neon canal walk, Glico sign photo — 5 minutes from the hotel.

places.name: Osaka Castle
places.description: The castle park is the highlight — nice at golden hour; museum inside is skippable if short on time.

places.name: Okonomiyaki & takoyaki crawl
places.description: Placeholder pick — okonomiyaki dinner around Dotonbori/Namba, takoyaki stands for dessert.

places.name: Senso-ji Temple
places.description: Tokyo's oldest temple, in Asakusa. Before 09:00 beats the crowds on Nakamise street.

places.name: Shibuya Crossing & Sky
places.description: The scramble crossing at dusk; Shibuya Sky observation deck needs advance tickets.

places.name: teamLab Planets
places.name_ja: チームラボプラネッツ
places.description: Immersive digital art in Toyosu. Book ~2 weeks ahead; you walk barefoot through water — wear shorts.

places.name: Ramen night in Shinjuku
places.description: Placeholder pick — Omoide Yokocho alleys are next to the hotel; ticket machines, cash only.

places.name: Don Quijote Kabukicho
places.description: Chaotic everything-store around the corner from the hotel — souvenirs, snacks, tax-free with passport.

places.name: Atami Sekaie
places.description: Oct 10 – 12 · Atami · Booking.com, confirmed, ₪6,768. Premium ocean-view ryokan — the pick for the Izu stop. A backup booking at Yuyado Ichibanchi (₪3,750, same dates) is still open — cancel it when you get a chance, both are free to cancel.

places.name: Kiunkaku
places.description: A 1919 seaside villa turned ryokan, now open to the public — gorgeous gardens and a coffee salon. A calm morning stop on the Izu day.

places.name: Atami Sun Beach & Ginza shotengai
places.name_ja: 熱海サンビーチ・熱海銀座
places.description: Palm-lined beach and the old shopping street right in town — easy on foot from the ryokan, good for a sunset wander in yukata.

places.name: MOA Museum of Art
places.description: Hilltop museum with sweeping sea views over Atami — one of three options for the Izu day (with the Jogasaki cliff walk and Shuzenji Onsen). Pick one.

places.name: Jogasaki Coastal Cliff Walk
places.description: Dramatic volcanic coastline on the Izukyu line, with a suspension bridge over the cliffs. One of three options for the Izu day (with MOA Museum and Shuzenji Onsen). Pick one.

places.name: Shuzenji Onsen
places.description: Bamboo forest walk and a 1,200-year-old temple in one of Izu's oldest onsen towns. One of three options for the Izu day (with MOA Museum and the Jogasaki cliff walk). Pick one.

places.name: Kinmedai & ise-ebi kaiseki
places.description: The local specialties — kinmedai (golden eye snapper) and ise-ebi spiny lobster, in season from October. Fresh Izu wasabi and sakura-ebi (cherry blossom shrimp) from Suruga Bay too. Best had as the ryokan's kaiseki dinner.

tips.body: Hakone Free Pass covers the whole loop (train, cable car, ropeway, pirate boat) and discounts many sights.
Use luggage forwarding (takkyubin) to send big bags ahead to a later hotel — travel the Fuji–Alps stretch light.
Fuji hides in clouds by late morning — plan viewpoints for early morning and check a Fuji visibility forecast.
Everything is walkable: station → Nakamachi street → castle in 20 minutes.
Hida beef is the local specialty — beef sushi at the market stalls, or a proper grill dinner.
The Kanazawa Loop Bus connects all the sights; day pass pays off with 3+ rides.
Buses get packed — prefer subway + walking; taxis are reasonable for 2 people on short hops.
Stand on the RIGHT on escalators in Osaka (opposite of Tokyo).
Get a Suica/Pasmo in Apple/Google Wallet for all trains, metro and convenience stores.
Trash cans are rare — carry a small bag for garbage.
Onsen etiquette: wash sitting down before entering the bath; towels stay out of the water.
Ask for a high floor on the Godzilla side; the head 'roars' on schedule from the 8F terrace.
Open 24h — sunrise or after 17:00 for photos without crowds.

Buy tickets the day they open (~Aug 8–14 for Oct 8). No booths at the park since May 2025 — online only, via Klook (foreign-card friendly). Premium Express passes sell out first, especially in Halloween season.

Express Pass Premium: if offered as P25 (incl. Space Fantasy) vs P29, prefer P25. With Premium, Nintendo World entry is guaranteed at any time. Passes are non-refundable, non-changeable and personal — no sharing.

Download the official USJ app for wait times, show times and the map. You can exit any queue before boarding. Check the crowd forecast at usjreal.asumirai.info (A=empty, F=packed). Save tickets as PDF + QR screenshots — signal is bad near the park.
Izu absorbs Pacific storms through October. If the forecast turns, stay north near Atami — Shimoda can get cut off.
Choose a room with a private open-air bath facing the sea if the budget allows — this is the trip's wind-down stretch.
Cancel the backup Yuyado Ichibanchi booking (Oct 10–12) when you get a chance — Atami Sekaie is the one you're keeping.

Ground rules for this itinerary: one timed anchor per day, never two. Start time varies with what actually opens that day, but never later than 10:00. Nothing scheduled after 20:00. Travel days count as light days, not as free days to fill.
Is there a private bath? Booking is offering an upgrade to a superior room with a private bath, which suggests the current one does not have it — and that was the point of Hakone.
Confirm parking at Mizno Hotel (Kawaguchiko).
Confirm parking at Onyado Nono (Matsumoto).
Confirm parking at Hotel Wood (Takayama).
Verify the out-of-prefecture drop-off fee on the car rental (picked up Odawara, returned Kanazawa).
International Driving Permit: 1949 Geneva Convention booklet format, issued by MEMSI. Valid 1 year from issue — check the date.
Visit Japan Web: register 2 weeks ahead, complete everything at least 6 hours before landing. One QR per person.

Passport on you, always. No passport, no tax-free and no Donki coupon. Takkyubin at every city change where you do not have the car: ~¥1,500-2,000 per suitcase, arrives next day, arrange at reception the night before. There are no rubbish bins — carry a small bag. No tipping, ever, anywhere. Don't eat while walking — stand next to the stall. Use 7-Eleven for cash withdrawals, not the airport exchange counters.

Download before flying: Suica in Apple Wallet (one each, Express Transit on), Google Maps with offline maps, Tabelog, GO (taxis), Airalo (eSIM), LINE, Payke, ChargeSpot, Japan Travel by Navitime, and the teamLab app.

Book this week: Ann Fragrance Asakusa (annfragrance.com/en) for Tue Sep 22. Kimono rental in Kyoto for Mon Oct 5 — ask for an 18:00 return. Omakase in Ginza for Wed Sep 23 (Tabelog / OMAKASE.in — some open 2 months out).

Book in August: Aug 16 — farewell dinner (Hakkoku or Aramaki) for Thu Oct 15, 60-day window, retry Sep 15 if monthly. Aug 20 — Sushi Kenshin Ebisu (say it's a birthday) for Sun Sep 20. Aug 21 — Maguro Mart Nakano for Mon Sep 21, opens exactly 1 month ahead, phone only, Japanese only, ask the hotel to call. Aug 23 — Omakase Ginza if not secured earlier. Aug 25 — Shinkansen Tokyo → Odawara for Fri Sep 25. Aug 29 — confirm ryokan dinner at Hotel Wood Takayama (29 Sep – 1 Oct).

Book in September: Sep 3 — Hokuriku Shinkansen + Thunderbird, both legs, for Sat Oct 3. Sep 5 — Enen Kyoto for Mon Oct 5. Sep 7 — Kintetsu Ltd Express Kyoto→Nara (optional, reserved seats) for Wed Oct 7. Sep 10 — Shinkansen Shin-Osaka → Atami for Sat Oct 10. Sep 12 — Shinkansen Atami → Tokyo for Mon Oct 12. Sep 15 — Shibuya Sky ~16:00 entry for Tue Oct 13, opens ~4 weeks ahead. Mid-Sep — Limousine Bus seat Shinjuku → Narita for Fri Oct 16, book at the hotel desk.

itinerary.title: Higashi Chaya in the late light
itinerary.note: Afternoon: Higashi Chaya in the late light.

itinerary.title: Refuel before handing it back or they charge a punitive rate. Out-of-prefecture…
itinerary.note: Refuel before handing it back or they charge a punitive rate. Out-of-prefecture returns usually have to land inside business hours (until ~20:00) — leave margin. Check the one-way drop-off fee is included in what you were quoted.

itinerary.title: Kenrokuen at opening
itinerary.note: Kenrokuen at opening — one of Japan's three great gardens. Castle next door.

itinerary.title: Omicho Market — kaisendon for lunch
itinerary.note: Omicho Market — kaisendon for lunch.

itinerary.title: Nagamachi samurai district, 21st Century Museum
itinerary.note: Nagamachi samurai district. 21st Century Museum (the swimming pool illusion).

itinerary.title: Higashi Chaya, gold-leaf ice cream
itinerary.note: Afternoon: back to Higashi Chaya, gold-leaf ice cream. Gold-leaf workshop if you fancy it.

itinerary.title: Hokuriku Shinkansen to Tsuruga, Thunderbird to Kyoto
itinerary.note: Hokuriku Shinkansen Kanazawa → Tsuruga, change to the Thunderbird → Kyoto (~2 h).

itinerary.title: Check in, central Kyoto (Shinmachi)
itinerary.note: Check in, central Kyoto (Shinmachi).

itinerary.title: Wander the neighbourhood with no plan
itinerary.note: Wander the neighbourhood with no plan: Nishiki in passing, a coffee, the Kamo River.

itinerary.title: Pontocho, first dinner in Kyoto
itinerary.note: Pontocho by the river, first dinner in Kyoto.

itinerary.title: Bamboo Grove — empty before 9:00
itinerary.note: Bamboo Grove — empty before 9:00, and that changes everything.

itinerary.title: Tenryu-ji and the Sogenchi garden
itinerary.note: Tenryu-ji and the Sogenchi garden.

itinerary.title: Togetsukyo Bridge, riverside walk, % Arabica
itinerary.note: Togetsukyo Bridge, riverside walk. % Arabica.

itinerary.title: Yudofu for lunch
itinerary.note: Yudofu for lunch.

itinerary.title: Kinkaku-ji and the dry garden at Ryoan-ji
itinerary.note: Kinkaku-ji and the dry garden at Ryoan-ji.

itinerary.title: Back to the centre, evening free
itinerary.note: Back to the centre. Evening free.

itinerary.title: Kimono — the only one of the trip
itinerary.note: Kimono — the only one of the trip.

itinerary.title: Fushimi Inari — climb 20 minutes
itinerary.note: Fushimi Inari — climb 20 minutes and the crowd disappears.

itinerary.title: Nishiki Market, Aritsugu knives
itinerary.note: Nishiki Market. Aritsugu (since 1560): buy a knife and they engrave your names in kanji.

itinerary.title: Kiyomizudera to Gion Hanamikoji
itinerary.note: Kiyomizudera → Sanneizaka → Ninenzaka → Yasaka Pagoda → Gion Hanamikoji.

itinerary.title: Enen — grilled wagyu
itinerary.note: Enen — grilled wagyu, order less than you think.

itinerary.title: When booking the kimono, ask for a plan with an 18:00 return (or next-morning return,…
itinerary.note: When booking the kimono, ask for a plan with an 18:00 return (or next-morning return, which several shops offer). A 17:30 return means you miss the sunset, which is the whole point of the day.

itinerary.title: Head out, eat before — no café inside
itinerary.note: Head out. Eat before — there's no café inside.

itinerary.title: teamLab Biovortex — budget 4 hours
itinerary.note: teamLab Biovortex — budget 4 hours, not 2. On entry, go down to the basement and hit the smaller rooms first.

itinerary.title: Lunch nearby
itinerary.note: Lunch nearby.

itinerary.title: Free afternoon
itinerary.note: Free afternoon: Philosopher's Path, Ginkaku-ji, a tea ceremony, or nothing.

itinerary.title: Kyoto farewell dinner
itinerary.note: Kyoto farewell dinner — Pontocho or Gion.

itinerary.title: This is not a two-hour visit. 10,000 m² over four floors, 50+ works, maze-like: 3…
itinerary.note: This is not a two-hour visit. 10,000 m² over four floors, 50+ works, maze-like: 3 hours is the sensible minimum and 4–5 if it's your first teamLab.

itinerary.title: 7 minutes on foot from the Hachijo East exit of Kyoto Station. Free lockers, no bags…
itinerary.note: 7 minutes on foot from the Hachijo East exit of Kyoto Station. Free lockers, no bags over 50 cm. Sneakers (there's an athletics area), plain light clothing for photos, no short skirts because of the mirrored floors.

itinerary.title: Nara — the one travel day that's a real day
Kintetsu Limited Express, Kyoto → Nara
itinerary.note: Kintetsu Limited Express, Kyoto → Nara (~45 min).

itinerary.title: Luggage into the lockers at Kintetsu Nara Station
itinerary.note: Luggage into the lockers at Kintetsu Nara Station.

itinerary.title: Nara Park — bow to the deer
itinerary.note: Nara Park — bow to the deer and they bow back.

itinerary.title: Todai-ji and the Great Buddha (728)
itinerary.note: Todai-ji and the Great Buddha (year 728).

itinerary.title: Lunch in Naramachi, Kasuga Taisha
itinerary.note: Lunch in Naramachi. Kasuga Taisha and its lantern paths if you still have legs.

itinerary.title: Kintetsu Nara → Osaka Namba (~40 min)
itinerary.note: Collect the luggage. Kintetsu Nara → Osaka Namba (~40 min).

itinerary.title: Check in at Candeo Shinsaibashi
itinerary.note: Check in at Candeo Shinsaibashi — ask for a high floor.

itinerary.title: Dotonbori at night
itinerary.note: Dotonbori at night — the Glico sign, the canal, the giant crab.

itinerary.title: Noguchi Taro Ramen Shinsaibashi
itinerary.note: Late: Noguchi Taro Ramen Shinsaibashi (17:00–04:00, no sign on the door, 5 min from the hotel).

itinerary.title: Kyoto → Nara → Osaka is all one Kintetsu line — no crossing the city, no changing…
itinerary.note: Kyoto → Nara → Osaka is all one Kintetsu line — no crossing the city, no changing operators. Namba drops you steps from the hotel.

itinerary.title: Luggage: simplest is the large lockers at Kintetsu Nara Station (~¥700). The…
itinerary.note: Luggage: simplest is the large lockers at Kintetsu Nara Station (~¥700). The alternative is takkyubin from the Kyoto hotel on the morning of the 6th — it reaches Osaka on the 7th — but then you need an overnight bag for the night of the 6th.

itinerary.title: There's a washing machine in the Osaka room. Use it.
itinerary.note: There's a washing machine in the Osaka room. Use it.

itinerary.title: Kuromon Market before midday
itinerary.note: Kuromon Market before midday — wagyu skewers, uni, scallops, fruit.

itinerary.title: Tennoji Park to Shinsekai
itinerary.note: Tennoji Park → Shinsekai: Tsutenkaku and the kushikatsu alleys.

itinerary.title: Den Den Town and Amerika-mura
itinerary.note: Den Den Town and Amerika-mura.

itinerary.title: Umeda Sky Building at sunset
itinerary.note: Umeda Sky Building at sunset — the open ring on the roof.

itinerary.title: Kushikatsu: never double-dip in the sauce. It's the only real rule.
itinerary.note: Kushikatsu: never double-dip in the sauce. It's the only real rule.

itinerary.title: Buffer day — sleep in if you're tired
itinerary.note: This is the trip's buffer. If you're tired, sleep in and walk around the neighbourhood — that's allowed.

itinerary.title: Options: Osaka Castle, Himeji, Kobe, or nothing
itinerary.note: If you have energy: Osaka Castle and its park, Himeji (1 h, the finest castle in Japan) or Kobe. If not: Sumiyoshi Taisha, the Kaiyukan aquarium, or nothing.

itinerary.title: Buy 551 Horai pork buns for tomorrow's train
itinerary.note: Buy 551 Horai pork buns for tomorrow's train.

itinerary.title: Takkyubin: big suitcases straight to the Tokyo hotel
itinerary.note: Takkyubin: big suitcases straight to the Tokyo hotel.

itinerary.title: Shinkansen Shin-Osaka → Atami (2:15)
itinerary.note: Shinkansen Shin-Osaka → Atami (2:15, change at Shin-Yokohama or Odawara).

itinerary.title: Check in at the ryokan, yukata
itinerary.note: Check in at the ryokan. Yukata.

itinerary.title: Atami Sun Beach and the Atami Ginza arcade
itinerary.note: Atami Sun Beach and the Atami Ginza arcade.

itinerary.title: Sea-view onsen at golden hour
itinerary.note: Sea-view onsen at golden hour.

itinerary.title: Kaiseki — kinmedai and ise-ebi
itinerary.note: Kaiseki at the ryokan — kinmedai, and ise-ebi, the lobster that comes into season right in October.

itinerary.title: Kiunkaku — 1919 villa, gardens, café room
itinerary.note: Kiunkaku — 1919 villa, beautiful gardens, café room.

itinerary.title: Pick one: MOA Museum / Jogasaki cliffs / Shuzenji Onsen
itinerary.note: Pick one: MOA Museum (up the hill, sea views) / Jogasaki cliffs / Shuzenji Onsen and its bamboo forest.

itinerary.title: Back to the ryokan, long onsen, second kaiseki
itinerary.note: Back to the ryokan. Long onsen. Second kaiseki. Nothing scheduled.

itinerary.title: Izu gets Pacific typhoons into October. If the forecast turns, stay close to Atami —…
itinerary.note: Izu gets Pacific typhoons into October. If the forecast turns, stay close to Atami — Shimoda can get cut off.

itinerary.title: Last onsen
itinerary.note: Last onsen.

itinerary.title: Shinkansen Atami → Tokyo (50 min)
itinerary.note: Shinkansen Atami → Tokyo (50 min).

itinerary.title: Check in at the Gracery, Kabukicho
itinerary.note: Check in at the Gracery, Kabukicho. Ask for a high floor away from the street — the area is loud until 3 or 4.

itinerary.title: Omoide Yokocho or Ramen Street
itinerary.note: Evening: Omoide Yokocho, yakitori in the alleys. Or Ramen Street at Tokyo Station.

itinerary.title: Coffee first, shops open 10:00–11:00
itinerary.note: Coffee first, shops open 10:00–11:00.

itinerary.title: Bic Camera — the ReFa
itinerary.note: Bic Camera — the ReFa. If you buy a hair dryer, insist on a 100–240V model; 100V ones burn out at home. Open the Bic Camera coupon on your phone before choosing.

itinerary.title: Don Quijote with the coupon
itinerary.note: Don Quijote with the coupon: donki.com/en → Service → Coupon. Live link, not a screenshot. Physical passport. Tax-free register.

itinerary.title: Drugstore haul
itinerary.note: Drugstore: sunscreen, sheet masks, Melano CC, Salonpas.

itinerary.title: Drop everything at the hotel
itinerary.note: Drop everything at the hotel.

itinerary.title: Shibuya: Gentle Monster
itinerary.note: Shibuya: Gentle Monster.

itinerary.title: Shibuya Sky — mid-October sunset ~17:05
itinerary.note: Shibuya Sky — mid-October sunset is around 17:05.

itinerary.title: Consumables get bought today, not earlier: they're sealed and you can't open them…
itinerary.note: Consumables get bought today, not earlier: they're sealed and you can't open them until you leave Japan.

itinerary.title: Stack the discounts: tax-free (min. ¥5,000) + Bic Camera coupon (5–7%) + Donki coupon…
itinerary.note: Stack the discounts: tax-free (min. ¥5,000) + Bic Camera coupon (5–7%) + Donki coupon + department store tourist card (~5%). Always confirm before the register.

itinerary.title: If the 13th is grey, move Shibuya Sky to the 14th — you have the day free.
itinerary.note: If the 13th is grey, move Shibuya Sky to the 14th — you have the day free.

itinerary.title: Yokohama — Chinatown, Cup Noodle Museum
itinerary.note: Pick one, or none: Yokohama — Chinatown, Cup Noodle Museum, Red Brick Warehouse. 30 min away.

itinerary.title: Hidden Tokyo — Yanaka, Shimokitazawa, Kagurazaka
itinerary.note: Hidden Tokyo — Yanaka and its pre-war lanes, vintage Shimokitazawa, Kagurazaka.

itinerary.title: Or nothing — it's day 26 of 27
itinerary.note: Nothing. It's day 26 of 27.

itinerary.title: Sleep in, last konbini breakfast
itinerary.note: Sleep in. Last konbini breakfast — you'll miss them more than you expect.

itinerary.title: Final souvenirs and a snack haul, pack
itinerary.note: Final souvenirs and a serious snack haul for home. Pack. Takkyubin can send the suitcases straight to the airport.

itinerary.title: Japan farewell dinner
itinerary.note: Japan farewell dinner.

itinerary.title: Check out 11:00, leave bags at the hotel
itinerary.note: Check out at 11:00, leave the bags at the hotel. Shinjuku Gyoen is 10 minutes away and it's the best place in the city to do nothing. Last shopping in Shinjuku, a good final lunch.

itinerary.title: Collect the bags and go
itinerary.note: Collect the bags and go. Limousine Bus direct from Shinjuku (85–120 min) or Narita Express (80 min). Be at the airport by 18:00. It's a Friday afternoon: leave margin for traffic. Book the bus seat at the hotel desk.
